replies.author: joelous
replies.body:
Usually when I'm making maps (this is really evident in my maps in particular):
1. I choose a shape; like a circle or square.
2. Mix other types of shape on top, moving it around. (I design it on paint)
3. Then add on random bits of path for gameplay (in the C;C series it was the double story layout)

replies.author: ProfessorUtonium
replies.body:
Start with the Basics.

Create an Outline of the Map.

Here is one of my maps that went through a lot: http://m.imgur.com/TvXiyIn

I first go through an outlining phase of the map then I start getting creative from there.

Once you reach a point where you like the final product, then finish the map http://imgur.com/a/T0lQN

Your map doesn't have to be all super complex and beautiful (I learned that when I made this map: https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/68e815417)

You just got to have the map be unique and creative from the others to get real attention from most mapdevs like me. The map needs to have pvp space and good gameplay such as platform placement or objective placement/structure placement. Just be yourself and start from the basics. If you ever want to build with someone, you can always ask.

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
Whenever I make a map, I don't really have any plans. I improvise, I make plans on the go.

However, you can make a mini-map layout for your map, It works. Especially if you want to make a tower or something.

Come on build sometime, you can help me make my map for Atlas. /mvtp ZinAnD if you wanna take a look-see and help me ;)
